newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert declines comment on Thomson sale.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert declines comment on Thomson sale.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert declined to comment on Thursday on the recapitalisation of Thomson SA and its sale to Lagardere Groupe. The European Commission had not been informed of either aspects, he said, refusing to comment only on press reports.

But Commission officials thought the injection of 11 billion French francs into the state-owned defence and consumer electronics group and its acquisition by Lagardere would have to examined under the European Union's state aid and merger rules respectively.
The French government announced on Wednesday it had chosen to sell Thomson to Lagardere and to inject 11 billion francs into the loss-making firm.
The deal will create the one of world's largest defence electronics firms after Lockheed-Martin-Loral of the United States by merging Thomson-CSF and Largardere's Matra.
Lagardere will have 60 percent of Thomson-Matra while the French state will have a golden share to safeguard national security interests.
The operation must get the approval of France's independent Privatisation Commission.
